summary: Frontend-only visual verification of HALL home-screen wireframe sphere across 5 viewports (desktop 1920x900, tablet 820x1180 & 768x1024, mobile 390x844 & 360x740). Inspected the iframe>canvas pixel-level content bounding box to confirm the sphere is NOT clipped at any edge. All viewports PASS: the sphere renders fully inside the square container with visible margin on all sides at every size. Horizontal-overflow check passes on all mobile viewports.

issues: Minor horizontal page overflow: at viewport 1920 scrollWidth=1984 (+64px); at viewport 820 scrollWidth=884 (+64px). Not sphere-related, outside this test scope, but worth flagging. Mobile widths (390, 360) and tablet 768 have NO horizontal overflow.

verification_details.methodology: For each viewport, located container '.hero > .relative', verified bounding box size matches CSS target (200/150/120), reached into iframe.contentDocument.canvas, scanned every pixel to compute content-bbox and derived margins to each canvas edge. Non-zero margin on all four sides = not clipped. Also captured clipped screenshots of the sphere region.

critical_code_review_comments: Proportional sphere sizing fix in wireframe-forms.tsx initSphere() works correctly across all tested viewports; sphere scales down proportionally and never clips the container.
Minor: at desktop/820 the page body has 64px horizontal overflow (not sphere-related). Suggest investigating other full-width elements if PO cares — not in scope for this fix.
context_for_next_testing_agent: The wireframe sphere container selector is `.hero > .relative`. To verify non-clipping, read the inner iframe canvas pixel data (same-origin srcDoc) and compute the bounding box of non-dark pixels; margins on all 4 edges must be > 0. Previous iteration confirmed proportional sizing fix (s = max(12, round(min(w,h)*0.24*len))) in /app/frontend/src/components/ui/wireframe-forms.tsx works. If page horizontal overflow on desktop/820 is reported, it is NOT from the sphere.
